doc.title: Wendy Oxenhorn interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 22, 2026

title: Loving blues as a child and the Raelette remark
summary: As a child she loved blues, Billie Holiday and Sinatra, and wanted to be a Raelette until her mother told her she was white.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: The melancholy came from two sources. One, how I even got the position and what I had been doing before that actually caused them to stand up and shake my hand at the job interview and say, “You’re it.” I had an interesting introduction to jazz. From the time I was a little kid I loved blues. I just loved blues and Billie Holiday, Frank Sinatra kind of jazz. And I used to listen with a transistor radio and swing on the swings and sing my heart out. You know. My biggest wish when I was like ten was to be a Raelette. You know ‘cause my parents used to love Ray Charles and listen and my mother one day like looked at me and she goes, “Wendy you can never be a Raelette.” I was like what? She goes, “You’re white.” And it was the first time in my life that I even realized that I wasn’t, you know, part of that club. And I remember, I remember being devastated you know. Because that’s really like that’s where I related. Those are the people I related to, that music was what I related to. I started out life as a ballerina.
